items.followUp: Define ecosystem and describe how its biotic and abiotic components interact.

rubric.why: A population is made up of organisms of the same species living in a particular area.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for both the same-species and same-area ideas; award 1 mark if only one is given.

rubric.why: A community consists of populations of different species living and interacting in an area.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for identifying different species' populations in the same area and their interaction; award 1 mark if one of these ideas is missing.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
A community consists of populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.

items.followUp: State four differences between an organ and an organ system.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus, while eukaryotic cells have one.
rubric.description: Compares the nucleus in the two cell types.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for correctly contrasting both cell types; award 1 mark for a correct statement about only one type.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles, whereas eukaryotic cells contain them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct contrast.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller and have 70S ribosomes; eukaryotic cells are generally larger and have 80S ribosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct comparison, such as size or ribosomes.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic DNA is usually circular and lies in the nucleoid; eukaryotic DNA is organized into linear chromosomes in the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct contrast in DNA or chromosome organization.

modelAnswer: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane bound nucleus; eukaryotic cells have a membrane bound nucleus.
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane bound organelles; eukaryotic cells contain membrane bound organelles.
Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller and have 70S ribosomes; eukaryotic cells are generally larger and have 80S ribosomes.
Prokaryotic DNA is usually circular and lies in the nucleoid; eukaryotic DNA is organized into linear chromosomes in the nucleus.

items.followUp: Write any four characteristics of viruses.

rubric.why: Enzymes are biological catalysts that increase the rate of biochemical reactions.
rubric.description: Identifies enzymes as biological catalysts that speed up reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying enzymes as biological catalysts or stating that they speed up reactions.

rubric.why: Enzymes are not used up in reactions and can be used again.
rubric.description: States that enzymes remain unchanged or can be reused.

rubric.why: Each enzyme acts on a particular substrate or reaction.
Enzymes are proteins and have optimum conditions for their activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes are proteins or that they have an optimum temperature or pH.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up biochemical reactions.
They are not consumed in the reactions and can be reused.
Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
Enzymes are proteins and work best at an optimum temperature and pH.

items.followUp: Describe the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis and identify where they take place.

rubric.why: A photosystem is a light-absorbing pigment-protein complex in the thylakoid membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a pigment-protein complex in the thylakoid membrane.

rubric.why: The Calvin cycle takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast.
rubric.description: States where the Calvin cycle occurs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the stroma.

rubric.why: Carbon dioxide is fixed to RuBP by RuBisCO, forming 3-PGA.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the fixation reactants or enzyme and the 3-PGA product.

rubric.why: ATP and NADPH are used to reduce 3-PGA to G3P.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking ATP and NADPH to the formation of G3P from 3-PGA.

rubric.why: Some G3P is used to form sugars, while the rest regenerates RuBP so the cycle can continue.
rubric.description: States the outcome of G3P formation or the regeneration step.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning sugar formation from G3P or regeneration of RuBP.

modelAnswer: A photosystem is a light-absorbing complex of pigments and proteins in the thylakoid membrane.
The Calvin cycle takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast.
Carbon dioxide combines with RuBP and is fixed by the enzyme RuBisCO, forming 3-PGA.
ATP and NADPH are used to reduce 3-PGA to G3P.
Some G3P is used to form sugars, while the rest regenerates RuBP using ATP, allowing the cycle to continue.

items.followUp: What are quantitative observations? Give one example.

rubric.why: Qualitative observations describe qualities rather than numerical measurements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that qualitative observations describe qualities or are non-numerical.

rubric.why: A suitable example describes a quality without giving a measurement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid non-numerical example.

modelAnswer: Qualitative observations describe the qualities or features of something without using numbers.
For example, a leaf is green.

rubric.why: Deductions are logical conclusions or inferences drawn from observations, often using prior knowledge.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for defining deductions as conclusions or inferences drawn from observations; award 1 mark for mentioning a conclusion or inference without linking it to observations.

modelAnswer: Deductions are logical conclusions drawn from observations, often using prior knowledge.
